newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW-NZ CPI data in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-NZ CPI data in line with expectations.

text.p: The following are economists' initial reactions to New Zealand Consumer Price Index statistics, which showed a 0.1 percent rise in the June quarter and a 1.1 percent rise in the June year.
DAVID PLANK, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST NEW ZEALAND
"Well in line with expectations, it's an excellent number that puts inflation at the mid-point of the Reserve Bank's band.
"It means the trend towards lower inflation is firmly established (and) annual inflation will continue to fall for the rest of this year."

He said the implication was clearly that the Reserve Bank will ease at some point over the next couple of months. "It's just a question of timing", but that time would now be more on the bank's side than if the CPI number had been a lower one that many in the money market had been positioning for.
"This number's given the bank some breathing space."

Plank said that monetary conditions would probably stabilise nearer the bank's preferred range, and he saw the MCI going back to 760/765 by the end of this week from about 755 before the data. "It means it's not going to go through 750," he added.
